name: Sticker Collage
visualIdentity: Cutout stickers sit on paper, notebook pages, or a simple surface with consistent white borders, light contact shadows, and slight rotation. The normalized label may differ from source wording.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to playful arrangements of existing subjects. Suggested fits include product or editorial introductions and illustrated narratives. Interactive HTML can make stickers buttons; with character or notebook hybrids, use focus or scroll to reveal expressions and annotations. Broader suitability is inferred.
limitations: Avoid stickers that float without surface contact, inconsistent cutout quality or border scale, and arbitrary shaking. Use another approach when the subject or story does not benefit from sticker arrangements. The palette and identity notes are suggestions, not canonical source colors.
palette: Optional new-artwork tokens: background #F3EBD9, foreground #273F49, white border #FFFFFF, coral #D78267, sage #77A397; five discrete colors, no gradient. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors exactly. Coral and sage are decorative only for normal text; their foreground contrast ratios are 3.844 and 3.945, below 4.5. Verify actual composited contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Place, peel, lift, repeat, and slightly rotate stickers with coherent contact shadows. Optional restrained entrance accents or bursts must preserve contact and seek deterministically. Video state follows shared composition time; scroll, hover, focus, and pointer input belong to interactive HTML. The optional chapter/story patterns require meaningful narrative states and readable holds; use only if supported by the content, with reversible progress.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping, synchronize to picture, and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Prepare cutouts with alpha masks; expand masks for uniform white borders and add light shadows. Keep border width consistent. Use supplied or authorized assets and exact copy; preserve approved artwork colors. SVG suits scalable shapes and masks; Python with Pillow, or Node.js with Sharp, can preprocess and composite assets. Other asset needs are unspecified.
combinations: Combine with style-025 doodle characters for expressive subjects: constant white border, foreground-ink linework, coral and sage fills only; no peach/mint fills, floating stickers, or arbitrary shaking. Combine with style-024 notebook annotations for guided notes: foreground ink, coral emphasis, short legible text, arrows on paper and clear of stickers. Avoid duplicate sticker-explainer styles. These are suggested pairings.
productionApproach: For video, use HyperFrames by default for assembly, seekable timing, synchronization, validation, and export; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, with reason recorded. SVG/PixiJS render visuals as needed; GSAP is the primary seekable timeline, with other motion tools optional and time-synchronized. Keep each animated property to one owner. Interactive HTML may bind progress to scroll or use focus/hover controls; include accessible labels and markup. Produce deterministic states, inspect representative frames and full playback, and verify audio, dimensions, timing, and loop continuity.
